A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TACO research, architecture, and core experiments. All pages, including Appendices A–C in v1 and A–D in v2, are readable and support matching text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original TabArena evaluations, training ablations, synthetic runtime and memory measurements, and MetroPT-3 chunking results.

after.justification: v2 reports revised original experiments, five-seed MetroPT-3 results, and additional TabFSBench and TableShift evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 adds self-supervised real-data adaptation using bootstrapped rows/features, randomly selected target columns, and discretization of continuous targets. This extends v1's synthetic-only training procedure. The compressor/predictor architecture, joint loss, and chunk-and-stitch inference remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained TabArena, MetroPT-3, and synthetic evaluations, v2 adds TabFSBench's single feature-shift regime and ID/OOD evaluation on 12 accessible TableShift datasets, including million-row datasets. It also introduces real-data adaptation, although the training datasets are not identified. These substantially extend training coverage and evaluation conditions.

E2.justification: New Figure 5 substantially broadens the TabArena comparison, including TabFlex, TabDPT, TabM, RealMLP, and classical learners. Tables 2 and 3 add XGBoost and AutoGluon comparisons; Table 3 also adds TabPFNv2 with random and kNN sampling. The earlier Random/kNN MetroPT-3 comparators are retained under explicit POT labels.

E3.justification: Training extends from 80k synthetic steps at length 1024 to longer-context continuation and real-data adaptation ending at 91k steps. The synthetic grid's reported compression changes from 4% to 1%. Table 3 replaces accuracy, log-loss, and ROC-AUC with precision and recall while retaining AUPRC; Tables 2/5 replace mean/median memory with first/subsequent prediction memory. Table 6 also changes retained-context counts, such as 120 to 100 for GiveMeSomeCredit. New Elo/tuning/ensembling and ID/OOD evaluations add further protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds substantial robustness analyses absent from v1: compression under single-feature shifts and ID versus OOD performance, alongside memory-feasibility testing on TableShift. The existing joint-versus-frozen, fixed-versus-multiple-rate, and chunking analyses remain, with some updated plotted distributions.

E5.justification: MetroPT-3 Table 3 changes from point estimates without a stated seed count to means and standard deviations over five seeds. This establishes newly reported replication and uncertainty, not an increase from a known earlier run count. Existing Friedman–Nemenyi tests and bootstrap confidence-interval practices remain.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 6, and 7 revise many results: Table 1's POT mean changes from 0.859 to 0.862 and TACO 1% from 0.854 to 0.855. Changed training and retained contexts prevent treating these as isolated same-setting gains. Reworked MetroPT-3 results show TACO AUPRC 0.8955, versus 0.9593 for XGBoost and 0.9656 for AutoGluon. Elo, shift, and first-prediction memory results are added. Existing TACO timing rows remain unchanged; the approximately 94× speedup was already reported at 1% in v1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2), the attention-complexity arguments, and Appendix B's chunk-size rule are unchanged. Section 3.1 makes the predictor's batch dimensions explicit, clarifying already-described batch prediction rather than adding substantive theory. Neither version contains new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion strengthen the quantitative efficiency claim from 53× speedup and 94% memory savings at 4% retained context to 94× and 98% at 1%, without statistically significant degradation. The abstract already advertised approximately 94× speedup, and the central compression and million-row chunking contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 5 identifies classification-only evaluation and limitations involving prior diversity, missingness, and temporal shifts, with regression/time-series extensions deferred. Appendix D adds interpretations about robustness and scalability. Some overreach the displayed evidence: Figure 18 does not connect TACO 1% and POT as statistically indistinguishable, and Table 8 does not show TACO having the strongest ANES accuracy.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release URL, specifies TabICLv1 as the synthetic-prior implementation, and documents continuation checkpoints and real-data task construction. Reported pretraining time changes from approximately 15 to 20 days on the same eight H100 GPUs. The real adaptation datasets remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for TabFSBench, TableShift, drift-resilient TabPFN, mesomorphic networks, and Mitra, and relates real-data adaptation to TabDPT's training procedure. The related-work narrative and end-to-end compression novelty claim remain largely unchanged. Publication updates to existing Jiang and Ye references are not new cited works.

P1.justification: Changes include localized rewriting in Section 3.1, expanded training descriptions, renaming research hypotheses to insights, and adding Limitations, an Impact Statement, and Appendix D. Author affiliation and proceedings text also change. Most existing prose and the narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Elo chart, a feature-shift CD diagram, and TableShift Table 8. It restructures MetroPT-3 Table 3 and memory headers in Tables 2/5, updates plot labels and styles, and adds visible dataset points to the detailed-results boxplots. These are localized additions and revisions within the retained layout; many other figures merely move or receive new numbers.

improvement.justification: v2 makes deployment tradeoffs clearer by exposing first-prediction memory, including 22.69 GB at 1% versus 549 MB subsequently, and strengthens MetroPT-3 evidence through five-seed reporting and stronger comparators. Added limitations and shift evaluations are useful. These gains are tempered by unsupported interpretations in Appendix D: Figure 18 contradicts blanket statistical parity, and Table 8 omits the XGBoost scores needed to verify its claimed performance parity.
